Our method, called the Similarity-Aware Annotation Reduction Network (SARN), aims to decrease the number of required annotations by identifying the most informative unannotated images that are closely related to the annotated dataset. This study aims to enhance the precision of $\beta$ decay spectra predictions by incorporating the effects of nuclear deformation, which is particularly significant for nuclei with prolate or oblate shapes. This research builds upon the existing $\beta$-decay code, $\beta$-decay nuclear model potential (BNMP), by incorporating the nuclear deformation parameter and the corresponding corrections to the single-particle energies and wave functions.   samples of functions $f$ in $X$ and corresponding outputs $Tf$ in $Y$.

  which facilitates efficient computation and minimizes the impact of noisy 
  training data.

  establishing the convergence of the algorithm. 
  Crucially, this convergence is achieved without relying on dense approximation 
  schemes, which is a significant innovation.

  involving operators and functions with diverse characteristics, including 
  compactly supported functions, functions with polynomial decay, 
  Sobolev spaces, and Besov spaces. 
  Our results provide a pioneering framework for learning operators between 
  function spaces, which we anticipate will serve as a foundation for 
  continued exploration in this area. 
  We also discuss the broader implications of our work, including its 
  potential applications to learning operators between Banach spaces and 
  between Hilbert spaces. 
  We conclude by highlighting several open research questions that arise from 
  our study.

Our proposed method, called Contrastive Label Propagation (CLAP), enhances the performance of semi-supervised image classification by leveraging the model's inherent ability to distinguish objects based on their inherent features. This work presents a novel, physics-driven image reconstruction approach called the 'k-space Total Generalized Gradient Space Sparse Reconstruction' (k-TGGSR) method.  Building on the Total Generalized Gradient Space Sparse Reconstruction (TGGSR) algorithm, k-TGGSR incorporates a data-driven prior derived from the under-sampled k-space data itself.  Specifically, k-TGGSR utilizes a learned generalized gradient space sparse representation of the under-sampled k-space data to regularize the reconstruction process.  This approach is evaluated using synthetic and real-world data sets acquired with reduced sampling rates.  Results show that k-TGGSR achieves comparable or superior image quality compared to state-of-the-art compressed sensing reconstruction methods.  This work demonstrates the potential of k-TGGSR to enhance MRI image reconstruction by effectively leveraging the inherent structure of under-sampled k-space data.
